Alex — great to meet earlier. Quick recap and next steps from our discovery:

- Scope: primary use is conversational assistant + summarization for knowledge base (consumer-facing + internal ops).
- Expected ramp: PoC (Q4): ~250M tokens/month; Scale (Q1): 800M–1.2B tokens/month.
- Key constraints: 99th %-ile latency < 300ms for short chat flows, strict PII controls (VPC), and target unit economics to justify build vs buy.

Two asks we discussed for Redwood to model pricing: 1) target $/1M tokens you're trying to hit, 2) preferred hosting mode (hosted API vs dedicated vs private) and any procurement windows.

I attached a baseline pricing worksheet (redwood_pricing_sheet_v3.xlsx) and a simple token-benchmark we use for comparisons. Can you confirm rough target $/1M and which month you expect to hit scale?

- Redwood to return a modeled comparison vs OpenAI / Anthropic / self-hosted within 48 hours

Thanks — Vanessa

Thanks Vanessa — good summary. A few quick data points from our side:

- Ramp timing: PoC Nov (250M/mo), full rollout Jan–Mar (target ~1B/mo).
- Current budgets: FY27 initial runway for this initiative is $60k–$120k/mo, but we need the unit economics to scale the program.
- Target unit price: we'd like to land at or below ~$400 per 1M tokens to make the ROI work across product lines.

For reference, we currently benchmarked a few options internally:
- OpenAI (managed endpoints): rough effective cost ~ $1,000–1,400 per 1M tokens depending on model mix and context lengths.
- Anthropic: in the same ballpark, ~ $800–1,200 per 1M tokens.
- Self-hosted on cloud (spot/auto-scale): our back-of-envelope is ~$250–$600 per 1M depending on utilization, reserved instances, and efficient KV caching.

Those are high-level; we don't have a rigorous comparison yet — appreciate Redwood's modeled view.

Also: procurement prefers hosted + dedicated reserved capacity if the SLA + price make sense. Procurement team copied.

Best — Alex

Alex — thanks for the numbers, very helpful. Quick notes on Redwood's modeled position and assumptions (see attached token_benchmark.xlsx for the math):

- Base assumptions: 1B tokens/month steady-state; mixed traffic 60% short chat (<=128 tokens), 40% long-context summarization (>=1024 tokens).
- Host comparisons (approx effective $/1M given our optimizations):
  - OpenAI (managed): ~$1,100 / 1M tokens (model-dependent; higher for larger context + GPT-4 class)
  - Anthropic (managed): ~$900 / 1M tokens
  - Self-host open models (cloud): ~$280–$520 / 1M tokens — range driven by utilization, reserved discounts, and batching/cache efficiency
  - Redwood hosted (baseline): ~$520 / 1M tokens for on-demand; with a reserved + batching profile we can get to ~$340 / 1M tokens for commitments at 1B/mo

Key levers to move to your $400 / 1M target:
- Reserved Dedicated capacity (commitments) — we model ~30–40% discount vs on-demand for predictable throughput
- KV/prefix caching and prompt engineering — reduces avg generated tokens per request and amplifies batching benefits
- Quantization + model selection — using optimized open models (8-bit/4-bit) when acceptable reduces inference cost materially

I've attached a worked example with your stated ramp and three pricing scenarios (on-demand, reserved, private). Can we schedule a 30m call Monday to walk through the spreadsheet and get procurement moving on a committed path?

If helpful, we can also run a short-hosted pilot (7–14 days) with live traffic mirroring to validate the effective $/1M and tail latency. That typically helps procurement commit faster.

Next steps suggested:
- Confirm Monday 9–9:30am PT or Tue 10–10:30am PT for 30m walkthrough
- I'll loop in an SE (Aditya) to prepare an optimized reserved proposal based on PoC metrics
- Provide a pilot scope doc and a simple SOW for procurement to review

Thanks — Vanessa
